title: Apify MCP Server
summary: Give your coding agent Apify's hosted MCP server to find Actors, run web scrapers and read their datasets, signing in with OAuth.
description: Apify is a platform of ready-made scrapers and automation programs called Actors. Its hosted MCP server lets an agent search the Apify Store, read an Actor's input schema, run it and fetch the results.

By default the server loads the Actor and docs tools plus web search and web fetch. Run storage, tasks, schedules and builds are off until you ask for them with a tools parameter on the URL, which keeps the surface small.
Running an Actor can use your Apify credits, so name the Actor and the limits in your prompt.
useWhen: Scrape a list of product pages into structured rows for a prototype
Search the Apify Store for an Actor that already does the job
Pull the dataset from a finished run into your test fixtures
Look up an Apify API detail without leaving the editor

mcp.name: apify
access: Searches the Apify Store and reads Actor details and Apify documentation
Runs Actors on your account, which can spend Apify credits, and reads their datasets
Limit the tools with ?tools= on the URL; the endpoint allows 20 requests per second per user

example.prompt: Find an Apify Actor that scrapes Google search results, run it for the query 'edge runtime benchmarks' with 10 results, and show me the titles.
example.result: Ran apify/google-search-scraper with maxPagesPerQuery 1. Ten results returned, the first being 'Edge runtime cold start benchmarks, 2026' with its URL and snippet. The dataset ID is attached for follow-up.

faq.question: Do I need an API token?
faq.answer: Not with OAuth, which opens a browser sign-in. A token is only needed for the bearer header option or for Apify's local npx server.

faq.question: Can I try it without an account?
faq.answer: Partly. If the tools parameter lists only search-actors, fetch-actor-details and the docs and API lookup tools, no token is required. Anything else needs sign-in.

faq.question: Why does call-actor not return my results?
faq.answer: It waits up to 45 seconds and returns run status and storage IDs. Follow it with get-dataset-items to read the data.
